To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the French government has implemented a policy of integration of Roma, which is not a real integration but an assimilation.
the Sénart experiment was a local Roma-targeted affirmative action which failed in its objective of “integrate” Roma without giving them political voice.
the French State is trying to integrate Roma by offering them housing and employment.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of the integration of Roma migrants and the way they have been integrated in a specific local context.
the question of the integration of Roma in the French society.
the analysis of a specific local policy which has been implemented since 2012 by the municipality of Sénart, a town located in the suburbs of Paris.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Roma migration is a consequence of the European integration process.
the Roma have been “forced” to move.
the “integration” of the Roma is not only an issue of “culture”, but also an issue of the Nation-State and of its political project.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

Roma are not a minority in France, but a population that has been made one by the French state, which has been using the Roma issue for its own purposes, and has been using the “Roma question” as a political tool in order to create an “imaginary” of the nation-state, which is supposed to be homogeneous, and in order to create a “Roma question”, which would be the opposite of that imaginary.
the Roma are the most discriminated group of Europe, and that they face a lot of difficulties in accessing to the labor market, to education and to housing.
Roma migrants are not only “victims” of their own culture, but also the victims of the policies of the nation-states they are living in.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Roma migrants are not only a population of migrants, but also a minority.

Roma migration to the West is not the consequence of the enactment of a nomadic culture but rather of the opportunities taken in a context where the European Union has been built on the basis of a “liberal” economic model which is not the only one possible.
the Roma are not a homogeneous community and their migration trajectories are highly differentiated.
